newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa's customs union neighbours -- Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland (BLNS) -- could lose more than one billion rand in crucial fiscal revenue if the proposed free trade accord between South African and the European Union was concluded.

- Trade unions, in an angry response to Land Affairs and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom's rejection of a minimum wage for the agricultural sector, have accused government of discriminating against workers.

- International Olympic Committee evaluation commission leader Thomas Back confirmed that although many of Cape Town's facilities included in the 2004 Olympic plan had yet to be built, this would not count against the city's chances of hosting the event.

- Industrial shares clawed back some of their losses on Friday as world markets breathed a sigh of relief after Friday's slump in response to Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on U.S. inflation.

- Police and Wildebeestfontein mine management were on Monday organising urgent meetings between two warring Freedom Park squatter settlement factions near Rustenburg in a bid to avoid further clashes in the conflict which claimed the lives of more than 30 residents at the weekend.
- South African telecommunications utility Telkom is expected to announce a sharp increase in local telephone tariffs on Wednesday as part of a move to eliminate local call rate subsidisation.

- A one billion rand entertainment complex next to the Fourways Mall on the outskirts of Johannesburg and consisting of a casino, hotels, restaurants and indoor and outdoor entertainment has been proposed by Tsogo Sun, a partnership between the Southern Sun Group and Tsogo Investments.

- Toco Holdings, the diversified industrial products and parking systems manufacturer, reported a net attributable loss on Monday for the six months to September 30 or 6.4 million rand, after earning 12.5 million last year.

- Retrieval of the bodies of the 16 miners entombed after a mudrush at the Rovic Diamond Mine -- owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc -- could take up to five months, during which time production will be unable to continue, a spokesman said on Monday.

- With only five days left for people to apply for amnesty, Truth and Reconciliation Committee chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutuhas made a public appeal to political leaders to stop confusing their followers about the amnesty process.
- President Nelson Mandela will sign South Africa's final constitution on Tuesday, ahead of its implementation early next year.

- Applying to host the Olympic Games meant taking part in the toughest competition which the Olympic movement could extend to the city -- and for every city taking part in the race there was only one medal on offer, and that was the gold.

These were the parting words of Dr Thomas Bach, chairman of the International Olympic Committee's evaluation commision, which on Monday wrapped up three days of intensive scrutiny of Cape Town's bid to stage the 2004 Games.
